programme.title: WWII: The Call of Duty
programme.desc: Worldwide, the conflict continued to escalate as Japan made their presence felt as signatories of the Tripartite Pact, giving Hitler's Axis of Evil more power. Britain stood alone as the nightly bombing raids of the Blitz devastated major cities.

programme.title: WWII: The Call of Duty
programme.desc: The only option for the German Sixth Army at Stalingrad was surrender, while all across Russia the Red Army consolidated their advantage. Also, as German cities encountered the kind of bombing that Britain faced back in 1940, courtesy of the RAF.

programme.title: WWII: The Call of Duty
programme.desc: While Hitler faced frustrations on all fronts, and the Japanese were kept at bay by the Americans, despite heavy US casualties, the Allied leaders faced a new challenge. Although Churchill and Roosevelt had always been comfortable working together, the Russian leader Joseph Stalin had in the past been regarded more as a foe than a friend.

programme.title: Visions of War: The Korean War
programme.desc: The Korean War - Brigadier General S.L.A. Marshall assesses the war and the effect it has had on training in today's army.

programme.title: First to Fight
programme.desc: The Marines break out from the Chosin Reservoir starting with the savage battle of East Hill.

programme.title: Broken Arrows: The Lost Bombs of the Cold War
programme.desc: On February 14th, 1950, a Convair B-36B plane crashed in northern British Colombia after jettisoning a Mark 4 nuclear bomb. This was the first such nuclear weapon loss in history. The Goldsboro B-52 crash was similar. Information newly declassified in 2013 showed that one of the bombs came very close to detonating which would have irreparably changed the North Carolina coastline.

programme.title: The Amazing World of War Machines
programme.desc: Since the end of World War II, when the United States dropped the A-bomb on Japan, and the advent of the Cold War, the threat of nuclear destruction has never seemed far away. Although in recent times attempts have been made to slow or even stop nuclear proliferation, countries such as North Korea, China and Pakistan have continued to develop and test their own missiles.

programme.title: The Crusade in Europe
programme.desc: This episode will take you on a brave campaign covering the Allied campaign in Italy from December 1943 to June 1944. We focus on the role of General Eisenhower as the Supreme Allied Commander and concluding with the victory in Rome.

programme.title: WWII: The Price of Empire
programme.desc: Russian troops enter Berlin; Hitler commits suicide; Third Reich accepts unconditional surrender.

programme.title: The Crusade in Europe
programme.desc: The episode explains how the Royal Air Force and the US Eighth Air Force helped win the war by bombing Germany day and night after the Battle of Britain.

programme.title: 3 Days in the Life of Lt. Kravtsov
programme.desc: The weight of unfairness looms over Lt. Kravtsov's fate. The prospect of dying at the tender age of eighteen seems unjust. As he embarks on his mission, the fragility of life and the enormity of his responsibility are inescapable.

programme.title: Auschwitz - Voices of 44 Survivors
programme.desc: For prisoners, life in camp was one of brutal forced labor, daily violence, hunger, thirst, disease and omnipresent death. In the midst of horror, everyone tried to find a way to survive...

programme.title: 3 Days in the Life of Lt. Kravtsov
programme.desc: Lt. Kravtsov's mission demands him to quickly assume command and guide his troops through treacherous circumstances. With limited time, he faces the immense challenge of maintaining morale, making tough decisions, and protecting his men in the face of overwhelming odds.

programme.title: Battlezone WWII: Arnhem and Over the Rhine
programme.desc: A Russian Captain and a German paratrooper recall the struggle to conquer Berlin in 1945.

programme.title: The US Battle For Supremacy In The Pacific
programme.desc: The activities of the 1st and 6th Marine Divisions on the island.

programme.title: The Attackers
programme.desc: The squadron prepares for a mission, mourns a fallen comrade, and faces chaos in the air. Inexperienced pilots break ranks, causing casualties. Personal relationships and inner struggles unfold amidst reprimands. The episode ends with consequences and regret.

programme.title: World of Warships Clash of Titans
programme.desc: Allied convoys resupplying the Soviet Union navigate the Arctic, infested with enemy aircraft.

programme.title: Soviet Storm
programme.desc: The capture of Rzhev, the city that connects all railroads in Western Russia, is imperative. It will cost the lives of some 3 million Soviet soldiers and 500 000 German soldiers. It will take the Soviets a total of 3 years to throw the Germans firmly out of the city. These bloodbaths will become known by the veterans and historians as 'The Rzhev Meat-Grinder'.

programme.title: Battlefields
programme.desc: August 26th, 1944, General de Gaulle has just returned to Paris. For the inhabitants of the capital, this is deliverance after four years of occupation. In ten days of combat, 1,000 resistant fell; 582 Parisians died; General Leclerc's 2nd Armored Division lost 141 men; the US forces also lost many men. Equally, 3,200 German soldiers also perished. Discover what actually happened in Paris.

programme.title: Soviet Storm
programme.desc: October 1941, Germany's Army Group Center is only some 25 km west of Moscow. The Russian winter, however, is only a few weeks away. With not enough soldiers or military equipment, the Soviet high command's only hope left is that the weather will save the capital. The battle ends in a bloody failure for the German Army, and it is forced to retreat.

programme.title: The Crusade in the Pacific
programme.desc: After World War II, Korea is divided along the 38th Parallel. In the North, the Soviet Union influences a Communist government under Kim Il-sung. In the South, the United States shepherds a young Republic. The Korean peninsula is plunged into war when North Korea invades the South.

programme.title: Patton's Finest Hour: The Battle Of The Bulge
programme.desc: Military career of the colorful General George S. Patton, with focus on his World War II action in Africa and Europe. A look at America's readiness for WWII.

programme.title: Secrets of the Nazis
programme.desc: In January 1945, the Soviet army discovered the existence of Auschwitz.

programme.title: Battlezone: The Korean War
programme.desc: Establishing the Lincoln Line... The need for blood in Korea... A powerful air-ground assault against the Reds. The Army Medical Corps is represented on this program with interviews with Nurse Captain Molly Younger, who served with a front line surgical team in Korea, and Sergeant Preputnick, who was an aid man with a rifle company in Korea.

programme.title: Battlefields
programme.desc: Verdun, February 21st, 1916. It is here that the most emblematic battle of the First World War will take place. Under the orders of General von Falkenhayn, chief of the General Staff of the Imperial armies, the Germans are determined to use the destructive power of their heavy artillery as much as possible to drown the French lines under a rain of fire.

programme.title: Hidden Side of World War II
programme.desc: This section takes a look behind the scenes at D-Day, revealing confidential decisions taken by the rulers, as well as the involvement of top-ranking officers and secret agents in the operations.

programme.title: WWII: The Call of Duty
programme.desc: With Britain failing to fall, the Blitz drew to a close, the sinking of the German battleship, the Bismarck, lifted the spirits of the British Navy. Hitler's campaign for Russia, Operation Barbarossa, got underway, the course of World War II changed.

programme.title: WWII: The Call of Duty
programme.desc: After success in North Africa the Allies returned to occupied Europe, first landing on Sicily before moving north into Italy under command of Montgomery, known fondly by his men as Monty. But as the Italians surrendered, the Germans occupied Rome.

programme.title: WWII: The Call of Duty
programme.desc: With Britain no longer facing Hitler alone, the first GIs arrived in the UK. As Singapore fell, the Allies looked on in horror as Japan also had control of Java, Burma and New Guinea, as they edged ever closer towards Australia.

programme.title: WWII: The Call of Duty
programme.desc: From the moment Adolf Hitler marched his troops into Poland on the 1st of September 1939, the Second World War was inevitable. As the opening skirmishes are played out, see for yourself the events that shaped the escalating crisis.

programme.title: Battlezone WWII: Nazi Blitzkrieg-The Battle For France

programme.title: Battlezone: The Gulf War
programme.desc: The ultimate test of tank technology is the battlefield. American tanks form the sharp end of the sword in Desert Storm. The U.S. marine corp was still using the older M-60 tank, although with some modifications.

programme.title: Blitzkrieg: The Lightning War
programme.desc: Poland invaded 1939, with the use of powerful archive film footage and highly detailed computer generated battle maps, charts the progress of a deprived post World War I Germany. We follow the rapid and spectacular military build-up, through to the largely horse-drawn invasions of Czechoslovakia and Poland.

programme.title: Impossible Peace

Militarism triumphs in Japan, which consolidates its invasion of China's north east. By the time the offices of president and chancellor have been combined into a single Fuhrer, Hitler has achieved absolute power in a one-party state without acting unconstitutionally.
